solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sadly, son, I can't give permission

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of son, I and can't are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A disappointed son is told that his request is refused.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to authorise or approve it officially.

clue.text: Stable and confident embracing rising church

indicators.note: embracing means the word for confident hugs the church letters inside it

parts.note: sure means confident

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising reads the church letters upwards, backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A believer is steady and assured as a church is built up.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure means firmly fixed and steady, not likely to give way.

clue.text: Old yet tipsily found after inn in a riot

indicators.note: the jumbled yet comes after the jumbled inn
a riot is disorder, so the letters of inn are rearranged
tipsily means drunkenly, staggering, so the letters of yet are mixed up

explanation.surface: An elderly reveller turns up drunk after a pub brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two anagram signals, 'in a riot' and 'tipsily', each mixing up one short word. 'found after' gives the order of the two jumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ninety years of age is decidedly elderly.

clue.text: Half of titans think deeply about ordinary little flier

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of the six letters of titans
about means the word for think deeply goes round the ordinary letter

parts.note: to muse is to ponder
O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Half the giants are pondering a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A titmouse is a small songbird, an old name for the tit.

clue.text: Boundless optimism in speech

indicators.note: boundless means without bounds, so the word's outer letters are dropped

parts.note: morale is confidence and optimism

explanation.surface: Unlimited hope expressed in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written.

clue.text: Attack very light, just opening

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical term for very, as in allegro assai

indicators.note: only the opening of the word light is wanted, its first letter

explanation.surface: A command to attack with a flare, a very light, just as things open up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very light' reads as a Very light, a signal flare, but 'very' is the musical direction ASSAI and 'just opening' takes L from 'light'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to set upon them violently, a synonym for attacking.

clue.text: Diamonds, for example, and gold for lover

parts.note: diamonds is one of the four suits of cards
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A man woos with diamonds and gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, a wooer.

clue.text: Tricky manoeuvre's skill whenever on skating rink, say

parts.note: art means skill
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'
a skating rink is an example of ice

explanation.surface: A skater's clever move shows skill whenever on the rink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is cunning trickery, a clever stratagem.

clue.text: Clear thinking with good fortune capturing thicko with no love for king

indicators.note: capturing means the new letters are taken into the word for lucky
for means in place of, so the king letter is swapped out

parts.note: lucky means having good fortune
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: no means the letter for love is left out of the word for thicko

parts.note: an idiot is a thicko, a stupid person
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A lucky clear thinker outwits a fool who has no love for the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops O from IDIOT to leave IDIT, which replaces K in LUCKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidity is clarity of thought and expression.

clue.text: Flog despicable person, pest seen down under

parts.note: to cane someone is to beat or flog them
a toad is a loathsome or contemptible person

explanation.surface: Someone wants to thrash a contemptible character, who turns out to be a nuisance in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The cane toad was introduced into Australia and has become a notorious invasive species there.

clue.text: Of organisms, one in horse parasite I primarily control

indicators.note: one goes in the parasite's name, placed within its letters

parts.note: a bot is the larva of the botfly, which infests horses
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of control is used

explanation.surface: A vet tells of fighting a parasite infecting a horse, with the speaker chiefly in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Biotic is the adjective for living things and the effects they have, relating to life and organisms.

clue.text: Pampered son accumulated entertaining dross essentially

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in a guest, holding a letter inside

parts.note: piled means heaped up

indicators.note: essentially picks the middle letter of dross

explanation.surface: A spoilt boy has hoarded rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoiled child has been indulged and overindulged.

clue.text: Restrict amount of drink essentially consumed in desert

indicators.note: the central letter is swallowed up inside the phrase for desert

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them

indicators.note: essentially picks the essence, the middle letter, of drink

explanation.surface: In the desert, how much you drink must be limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy waste but is the verb RAT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration something is to limit how much of it each person may have.

clue.text: Tricked involving end of lesson taught without challenge

indicators.note: involving means the tricked word takes the other letter into itself

parts.note: spoofed means hoaxed or tricked

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of lesson is used

explanation.surface: A pupil was fooled at the close of a lesson and taught nothing demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoon-fed teaching hands over information so the learner never has to think or struggle.

clue.text: Regrets holding key but frees from captivity

indicators.note: holding means the word for regrets takes the key inside it

parts.note: rues means regrets
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A captor has regrets but lets the captive go.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescues means saves someone from danger or confinement.

clue.text: Article rejected quotes about conservative man leading disciplined life

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: rejected suggests being sent back, so the word for quotes with its contents runs backwards
about means the word for quotes goes around the conservative letter

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: A newspaper article declined to quote a Conservative who lives austerely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses CITES with C inside, CITECS, to SCETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic is a person who practises severe self-denial, usually for religious reasons.

clue.text: Leave droppings

definitions.meaning: an order to go away at once
animal excrement, as tracked by naturalists

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave behind animal dung.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat serves both as a shooing command to depart and as the naturalists' word for animal faeces.

clue.text: Treasonous face admitting nothing in cunning

indicators.note: admitting means letting the cunning word with its contents inside the word for face

parts.note: dial is slang for face

indicators.note: in means the nothing letter goes inside the word for cunning

parts.note: sly means cunning
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A traitor's face shows sly guile.
explanation.definitionFit: Disloyal means unfaithful to one's country or allegiance, as treason is.

clue.text: After confused agitation, sailor gets biscuit

indicators.note: after means the sailor comes after the agitation in the answer

parts.note: a flap is a state of agitated panic
jack is a traditional name for a sailor, as in Jack Tar

explanation.surface: Having calmed his nerves, a seaman tucks into a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapjack in Britain is a chewy oat bar or biscuit made with syrup.

clue.text: Put in motion part four of drama at Globe finally

parts.note: Act IV is the fourth act of a play
taken as written

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Globe

explanation.surface: The fourth act of a play gets going at the Globe theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe is Shakespeare's theatre in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate something is to set it working or start it.

clue.text: Afraid leather disguises having nothing on?

indicators.note: the two words conceal the answer within them, a disguise over the letters

explanation.surface: Someone scared of leather covers up, suggesting a nudist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having nothing on' suggests nakedness, but means having no engagements; the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idle is unoccupied, with no tasks or appointments in the diary.

clue.text: Discipline of type of fiction

definitions.meaning: a branch of knowledge or field of study
... fiction is a genre, so ... names a type of fiction

explanation.surface: A literary genre is imposing order on itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a part: SCIENCE comes before 'fiction' to name the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic fields of study are called disciplines, and physics or chemistry is a science.

clue.text: Fall in drops and drips regularly lit up

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of drips, first third and fifth
in a down entry, up means the word lit reads upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Water drips steadily from a lit ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: To distil can mean to trickle or fall in drops, as in distillation.

clue.text: Incarnation of backsliding renegade, a vice-admiral

indicators.note: backsliding suggests going backwards, so all the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or turncoat
taken as written
VA is the abbreviation for vice-admiral

explanation.surface: A turncoat naval officer slips back into bad ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the incarnation of a Hindu deity in earthly form.

clue.text: Marriage partner introducing grand game

indicators.note: introducing means the grand letter is brought into the word for marriage partner

parts.note: a bride is a partner in a marriage
G is an abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A spouse brings out a big card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is a card game for four players in partnerships.

clue.text: Odd piles, curiously off balance

indicators.note: curiously means arranged in a strange way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely heaped stacks are tilting dangerously.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lopsided leans to one side, uneven and unstable in weight.

clue.text: Metal splinter left moving nearer to heart

indicators.note: the letter for left is shifted inward, closer to the centre of the word for splinter

parts.note: a sliver is a thin splinter

explanation.surface: A metal shard works its way towards a patient's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving nearer to heart' shifts L one place inward, SLIVER to SILVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is a precious metallic element, symbol Ag.

clue.text: Limit animal flesh, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals what follows is a word that is heard, a soundalike

parts.note: meat is animal flesh

explanation.surface: We are told to limit how much meat we eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mete is an old word for a boundary or limit, as in metes and bounds.

clue.text: Indeed, once pig pen could be characterised by upheaval

parts.note: yea is an archaic word for yes or indeed
a sty is an enclosure for pigs

explanation.surface: A farmer muses that a pigsty, once, was a scene of turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty, from fermenting yeast, can mean frothy, agitated or turbulent.

clue.text: In a frenzy: pet adder's gone

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild disorder, so the letters of pet adder are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A pet snake has thrashed about wildly and escaped.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Departed means having left, or euphemistically having died.

clue.text: Credible as beginnings of legal year

parts.note: like can mean as, in the same way as

indicators.note: beginnings of takes the opening letter of each of legal and year

explanation.surface: A lawyer judges plausible the way a legal year starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something likely is probable and so plausible.

clue.text: Train engineers transport for late passengers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
a hearse carries the dead, the late

explanation.surface: A rail company's engineers lay on a train for passengers who missed the last one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not tardy, so the transport is a hearse.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise or drill, as actors train for a performance.
